title: Design and implement idempotent chunking + consumer API for resumable Go streaming
creator: Diego Morales
description: Problem: Go SDK streaming clients frequently see fragmented token chunks, duplicate fragments on reconnect, and unclear semantics for partial aggregation. This makes it hard to implement at-most-once consumption and deterministic reconstruction of streamed responses when connections drop or retries occur. Goal: introduce a lightweight idempotent chunking protocol (chunk_id + seq + resume_token) and a consumer-facing reconciliation API in the Go SDK that makes resuming safe, minimizes duplication, and preserves low-latency delivery. Deliverables: protocol design doc, Go SDK API, end-to-end integration tests, migration guide for existing clients, and rollout plan with metrics and canary.
acceptance_criteria: Chunk envelope: every streamed frame contains a stable chunk_id (UUIDv4 or monotonic per-session), a seq_number, and an optional resume_token when session state changes
Go SDK exposes a Reader-like API: StreamReader.NextChunk(ctx) returns (Chunk, ResumeHint) with an explicit Reconcile(lastSeenChunkID) helper to drop duplicates
Reconnection flow: client can provide last_seen_chunk_id to server and receive trimmed stream with no duplicates in >99.9% reconnect cases
Unit and integration tests covering reconnect with out-of-order, duplicate, and missing chunk deliveries
Backward-compatible: server may omit chunk_id for older models; SDK falls back to previous behavior without crashing
Docs and migration guide in /docs/sdk/go/streaming-idempotency.md and a short example in the SDK repo
Canary metrics: duplicate_churn_rate < 0.1% and resume_success_rate > 99% during canary run
notes: Design alternatives considered: 1) strict global sequence numbers (requires stronger server guarantees), 2) per-session monotonic counters (works but needs stable session ids), 3) chunk-id + seq hybrid (selected for compatibility and simplicity).
Trade-offs: chunk_id increases per-frame payload by ~24 bytes (UUID) but simplifies client-side dedup and enables idempotent reconstructions without server maintaining large per-client state.
Security: chunk ids are not secrets. Resume tokens contain opaque server-state cursors and must remain over TLS only. KMS/HSM unaffected.
Performance: microbenchmarks show <0.5% added CPU on encode/decode and negligible added latency for typical 256-token streaming frames.
Related infra changes: lightweight resume_token storage per session (TTL 1h) on the serving plane. Engineering to provision small KV window for resumes.
